type: position = s16 * 2^-frac, frac being the first word of the block's 32-byte fraction header (the GX vertex attribute table shift); normals s8 with frac 6 (64 = 1.0, unit length verified), texture coordinates s16 with frac 14 (16384 = 1.0). World chunks use frac 6 in world space; placed props use 7..10 in the model's local space (a 1-unit coin: 10; a 6-unit sunflower: 10; a 10-unit windmill blade set: 10)
structure: Tutorial: frac 6 x1589, 7 x19, 8 x16, 9 x9, 10 x631. Mining: 6 x641, 9 x2, 10 x282.

location.offset: fraction header at the 32-aligned position after a block's arrays; tutorial block 0 {6,14,0,0}, block #1586 {10,6,14,14}, block #1859 {10,6,14,14,14,0,0,0}

meaning: How the stored integers become coordinates. The check is against the owner's declared bounds ({4, 1, min xyz, max xyz} attribute of the node record): with the header's fraction, world chunk #2 dequantises to x -220.17..-218.64 against a declared box of -220.17..-218.64, a 0.01-unit error; per model, 209 of 209 tutorial models and 131 of 131 Mining models with declared bounds have every vertex inside them at 5%. A fixed fraction guessed from the extent would not do: the two kinds differ, and the props differ among themselves.
